issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is derived from Theorems sec3:thm2 and sec4:thm1 via Slutsky, which requires the limiting covariance $\Xi^\star$ to be nonsingular (chi-square limit of $(\bx-\bx_t)^T\hat\Xi_t^{-1}(\bx-\bx_t)/\baralpha_t$) and $\bw^T\Xi^\star\bw>0$ for the interval statement. None of Assumptions 1–4 guarantees that $\mE[\nabla f(\bx^\star;\xi)\nabla^T f(\bx^\star;\xi)]$ (hence $\Omega^\star$, $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^\star$) is positive definite; if it is singular in some direction, $\hat\Xi_t$ has vanishing eigenvalues in the limit, $\hat\Xi_t^{-1}$ is not asymptotically controlled and the studentized statistics are degenerate 0/0 ratios, so the stated coverage limits do not follow. No proof of the corollary is provided ("immediately implies").
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis $\mE[\nabla f(\bx^\star;\xi)\nabla^T f(\bx^\star;\xi)]\succ 0$ (which, via $I-C^\star\succeq(1-\rho^\tau)I$, yields $\Lambda\succ0$ and $\Xi^\star\succ0$) and invoke Slutsky's theorem explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The coverage guarantees of Corollary sec4:cor1 (confidence regions and directional intervals) are not established in the stated generality; they hold only under an additional nondegeneracy condition on the gradient covariance at $\bx^\star$.
issues.title: Corollary on confidence regions/intervals omits a nondegeneracy hypothesis guaranteeing that Xi* is invertible (and w^T Xi* w > 0)
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition restores every advertised guarantee with a routine argument; no rate, method, or scope is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Appendix A correctly derives $\hat\Xi_{t+1}=\frac{t}{t+1}(\hat\Xi_t+R_t\Lambda_tR_t^T)$ and the Woodbury update with $\Lambda_t^{-1}$. Inverting $\Lambda_t$ gives $\Lambda_t^{-1}=(-a_t,1,0;1,0,0;0,0,t\varphi_t)$ (the $2\times2$ block $(0,1;1,a_t)$ has inverse $(-a_t,1;1,0)$). The main text instead states $\Pi_t=(a_t,1,0;1,0,0;0,0,t\varphi_t)$ with $+a_t$, so the displayed recursion computes a matrix different from $\hat\Xi_{t+1}^{-1}$ whenever $a_t\neq0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the (1,1) entry of $\Pi_t$ by $-a_t$, i.e., $\Pi_t=\Lambda_t^{-1}=(-a_t,1,0;1,0,0;0,0,t\varphi_t)$.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit online recursion for $\hat\Xi_t^{-1}$ used to construct the confidence region in Section 4.2 is incorrect as printed; the estimator itself and its theory are unaffected.
issues.title: Sign error in the matrix $\Pi_t$ of the online update of $\hat\Xi_t^{-1}$
issues.why_classification: A single local correction, already implied by the appendix derivation, restores the update; no result or guarantee is lost.

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does~not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to~the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.overall_effect: The advertised applicability of the consistency guarantee to conditioned SGD / preconditioned methods with non-Hessian $B_t$ is not established; only the sketched Newton setting with Hessian averaging is covered by Theorem sec4:thm1.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that Theorem sec4:thm1 applies to conditioned SGD without $B_t$ converging to the true Hessian
issues.why_classification: The main results survive intact, but the claimed extension either must be dropped (loss of an advertised scope) or requires a contained but nontrivial new argument; it is not a one-line fix nor does it undermine the core theorems.
